sourceFacts.analysis: Core callbacks follow creation/start/resume and pause/stop/destroy with restart; visible paused multi-window resources require matched start/stop or resume/pause acquisition/release.
Pause is brief and unsuitable for user data/network/database save work; foreground save opportunities and stop fallback are described without a durable-write guarantee.
System kills the containing process, not an individual activity; the table is conditional on absence of other components; instance state is small transient state requiring main-thread serialization.
Same-process A pause precedes B create/start/resume and then invisible A stop; modern external activity-result API is recommended, while the earlier section still names legacy startActivityForResult.

Compose lifecycle-aware collection is recommended; annotation observer snippets and Compose recommendations coexist; all displayed snippets and resource-link list were read without inferring linked reference completion.

sourceFacts.analysis: ViewModel survives configuration change but not process death; system saved state survives system process death but not user dismissal, while persistent storage can survive both.
Saved state is small transient data; stop captures state and stopped writes need another start/stop; large app data belongs in local storage.
Registry provider returns a Bundle; key registration/consume occurs after super.onCreate or ON_CREATE; the displayed second sample declares query as val then reassigns it.
Local persistence lasts while app remains installed unless app data is cleared; none of ViewModel/rememberSaveable/SavedStateHandle replaces long-term app storage.
Model data and small query restore differently after process death versus configuration change; first creation has empty restored state; additional resource titles are not child-body reading.

sourceFacts.analysis: Android system determines process lifetime using active components, user importance and memory; foreground, visible, service and cached importance hierarchy is described.
Returning from a receiver after starting an unmanaged thread can leave its process killable; a scheduled job is suggested so system knows work remains.
Cached processes should stop work, may receive little/no execution time from Android13 and can be killed without onDestroy; exact cached ordering is a platform implementation detail.
Most important active component and bound-service/content-provider dependencies can raise process importance; priority is not a durable job guarantee.

sourceFacts.analysis: WorkManager signals important long-running work with managed foreground service and notification; keep-alive is qualified rather than guaranteed.
Android16 foreground-service workers still use JobScheduler and may exhaust quota; direct FGS/user-initiated transfer are suggestions requiring further eligibility analysis.
CoroutineWorker.setForeground is suspending; Worker/ListenableWorker.setForegroundAsync returns ListenableFuture<Void>; cancel PendingIntent support is described from2.3.0-alpha03.

Target API34+ requires service type for long workers; target29 location and30 camera/microphone cases are separately stated; type must be declared in manifest and passed at runtime with prerequisites checked.

readOnlyCodeComparisons.analysis: Document/history/dirty in memory Map; save awaits write then updates saved baseline; no Android restoration proof.
Command/client Maps with request-ID dedup and time-limited cleanup; no durable process-restart receipt contract in this read class.
Build job Map, AbortController and close cancellation are process-local; output success and job restoration are distinct.
Session Map, compiler staging/cache commit, queued RPC and process close; Windows/native worker support is not Android compiler/service support.
Windows job owns server child with kill-on-close; this is not an Android process-lifetime implementation.

hbDecisionScope: Proposed contracts only, no callable implementation added; human/C++/node/AI share durable IDs, typed values, revision protection, attempt epochs and receipts.
